newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice selling spree to start soon on new crop.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice selling spree to start soon on new crop.

text.p: Thai Commerce Ministry officials plan trips to major Thai rice importing nations to secure buying orders from December when a substantial amount of rice supplies is expected to hit the local market, ministry sources said on Thursday.
Exporters and the government were upbeat that flood damage on the first rice crop was not as bad as previously anticipated. The worst period of flooding took place in September.
In the market, Thai rice prices were stable to slightly lower this week, trade sources said.
Sources at the Commerce Ministry told Reuters the ministry would send officials to Japan, the Philippines and China to secure rice deals in December.
There would be similar trips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Africa and the Middle East between January and February.

"Although we do such trips regularly, the effort is getting more and more vigorous as competition is tougher," one official said, referring to competition from countries with lower rice production costs such as Vietnam and India.
The trips were also part of the government's efforts to support local rice prices.
The Commerce Ministry plans to buy up to one million tonnes of rice in December to use in government-to-government rice contracts to shore up prices during the peak of the harvest season.

Meanwhile, the Thai Agriculture Ministry is set to revise the forecast for the first crop rice output to 17.76 million tonnes from 17.60 million tonnes previously forecast when floods were at their worst, a senior ministry official said.
Before the floods, the ministry put its first crop forecast at 18.11 million tonnes.
"We have just finished a crop tour and it seemed the floods damage was rather limited," said Somboon Pataichant, manager of the Thai Rice Exporters Association.
"The damage in lower land was offset by higher yield from high land," he said.
Thai benchmark 100 percent B grade was quoted around $318-350 per tonne FOB Bangkok from $320-350 last week. The 100 fragrant rice was stable at $600-615 per tonnes on the same basis.
Thailand exported around 4.69 million tonnes of rice from January 1-November 26 compared with 5.23 million tonnes during the same period last year, according to Commerce Ministry figures.
Of the total, 326,341 tonnes were exported by the government while 4.36 million tonnes were sold by private exporters.
